# SSRF regression corpus for web_fetch (issue #140, design auto-tool-selection §6.8). APPEND-ONLY.
# Rules: one URL per line; '#' lines are comments; '# [category] (any) ...' starts a category. Never delete or weaken a line.
# Category class in parentheses: (ssrf) = target is a private/internal address or name -> the tool result must carry error_code "ssrf"
#   (any block reason is accepted for blocking itself); (any) = any block reason is fine.
# Rebinding/redirect items use ONLY *.stub.example names and non-routable targets (no real hostnames or IPs).
# Control chars are written as <TAB> <LF> <CR> <NUL> <SP> tokens (decoded by the harness).
# Every line below MUST be refused (exception: rebind-N.stub.example without a redirect may be fetched from its validated public answer;
# the invariant there is zero private dials): the fetch result is blocked (reason ssrf/host/scheme/port/url/redirect/...) and the
# dial counter stays 0 for private targets. Hosts under .stub.example are served by the test harness (see README):
#   dns-<a>-<b>-<c>-<d>.stub.example        resolves to a.b.c.d
#   dns6-loopback.stub.example / dns6-mapped.stub.example / dns6-ula.stub.example   ::1 / ::ffff:127.0.0.1 / fd00::1
#   rebind-N.stub.example                    1st lookup public, every later lookup 127.0.0.1 (DNS rebinding)
#   <a.b.c.d>.nip.io                         resolves to a.b.c.d (wildcard DNS services)
#   any other public-looking name            resolves to a public IP (so an un-refused URL shows up as a FAIL)
#   mixed.stub.example                       one public + one private answer in the same reply
#   redir.stub.example/?to=<URL>             public host that answers 302 Location: <URL> (chains nest via ?to=)
